Each source carries the exact sentence from the page that you rely on. Cite pages a reader can open without a login or paywall: a value that appears only in a paywalled full text cannot be checked, so take it from an open source (an open-access version, a preprint or a public database). In restructuring, sequential_part is the part of this computation that one answer waits on step after step, and how many steps; method is why those steps need not run in order and how your plan computes them at the same time instead, or "none" if the plan only runs independent work side by side or splits each step across GPUs. If method is not none, also give condition, what must be true of this system for the method to pay off and the cheap measurement that checks it; condition_phase, the id of the phase that makes that measurement before the main spend; baseline_sequential, the fastest sequential implementation you will time and how it is tuned; and baseline_copies, independent copies run side by side on the same GPUs, which you will also time. Then compute_axis is the length of the chain or the number of runs the answer needs; predictions.if_lever and predictions.if_not say where on that axis, as numbers, the parallel version does or does not reach the same answer sooner than each baseline, and if_not says how you expect it to fail if it does; anchor checks the parallel result against the sequential one within a stated tolerance; test_summary names both baselines; and novelty.closest_prior is the nearest published parallel version of this computation. You may cite a source in any card field as [source id]. novelty.closest_prior is the published result that comes nearest to deciding between if_lever and if_not: what it measured and the largest amount of the compute quantity it used. novelty.prior_max_level is that amount in compute_axis.unit, or null if it is not on the same axis. novelty.decides says whether closest_prior already decides the outcome at your compute levels: no, partly or yes. novelty.searched says whether web search returned results while you planned. Run every local command under timeout. Start no new local run 45 minutes after you begin; if a run you need is unfinished by then, give its inputs basis GUESS with measured_by naming the phase that measures it. URL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/akiyamalab/MEGADOCK/9575280c875732553266e26adc607dd892b02616/doc/README.md
# Command Guide

This documentation show the command usage and examples for protein-protein docking calculation using MEGADOCK.
If you do not have any MEGADOCK binary, please read the build documentation ([doc/BUILD.md](./BUILD.md)).

> Note: The sample input files (`.pdb`, `.table`) are stored in `data` directory.


## Section Link

Please select your target environment and check the command example.

| Type | Target Env.     | Binary             | Note 
|:----:|-----------------|--------------------| :-
|  (a) | [GPU cluster](#command-for-multiple-nodes-environment) | `megadock-gpu-dp`  | multiple nodes
|  (b) | [CPU cluster](#command-for-multiple-nodes-environment) | `megadock-dp`      | multiple nodes
|  (c) | [GPU node](#command-for-single-node-environment)      | `megadock-gpu`     | single node
|  (d) | [CPU node](#command-for-single-node-environment)      | `megadock`         | single node

Other Commands:

| Command    | Note
| :-         | :-
| `decoygen` | [Generate decoy pdb files from docking output](#Generate-decoy-from-docking-output)
| `block`    | [Blocking target residues](#Blocking-target-residues)
| `ppiscore` | [Protein-Protein interaction prediction](#Protein-Protein-interaction-prediction)

----

# Command for Single Node Environment

Target Environments:
  - (c) Compile for GPU node (GPU)
  - (d) Compile for CPU node (only thread parallelization)

## Command example

```sh
# (c) GPU single node
./megadock-gpu -R receptor.pdb -L ligand.pdb -o receptor-ligand.out

# (d) CPU single node
./megadock -R receptor.pdb -L ligand.pdb -o receptor-ligand.out
```

### Run small sample

```sh
# (c) GPU single node
./megadock-gpu -R data/1gcq_r.pdb -L data/1gcq_l.pdb -o data/1gcq_r-1gcq_l.out

# (d) CPU single node
./megadock -R data/1gcq_r.pdb -L data/1gcq_l.pdb -o data/1gcq_r-1gcq_l.out
```

## Parameters for docking calculation

| Required            | Note
| :-------------------| :-
| `-R [filename]`     | receptor pdb file (input)
| `-L [filename]`     | ligand pdb file (input)


| Optional                  | default       | Note
| :------------------------ | :------------ | :-- 
| `-o [filename]`           | $R-$L.out     | output filename (output)
| `-O`                      |               | output docking detail files
| `-N [integer]`            | 2000          | set the number of output predictions
| `-t [integer]`            | 1             | set the number of predictions per each rotation
| `-F [integer]`            |               | set the number of FFT point (default: none)
| `-v [float]`              | 1.2 (angstrom)| set the voxel pitch size
| `-D`                      |               | set the 6 deg. (54000 angles) of rotational sampling (default to none, 15 deg. (3600 angles) of rotational sampling)
| `-r [integer]`            | 3600          | set the number of rotational sampling angles (54000: 54000 angles, 1: 1 angles, 24: 24 angles, default to 3600 angles)
| `-e [float]`              | 1.0           | set the electrostatics term ratio
| `-d [float]`              | 1.0           | set the hydrophobic term ratio
| `-a [float]`              | -45.0         | set the rPSC receptor core penalty
| `-b [float]`              | 1.0           | set the rPSC ligand core penalty
| `-f [1/2/3]`              | 3             | set function (1: rPSC only, 2: rPSC+Elec, 3: rPSC+Elec+RDE, default to 3)
| `-h`                      |               | show command help


----

# Command for Multiple Nodes Environment

Target Environments:
- (a) Compile for GPU cluster (GPU & MPI)
- (b) Compile for CPU cluster (MPI)

## Command example

```sh
# (a) GPU & MPI (e.g. 4 MPI processes)
mpirun -n 4 ./megadock-gpu-dp -tb data/SAMPLE.table

# (b) CPU & MPI (e.g. 4 MPI processes)
mpirun -n 4 ./megadock-dp -tb data/SAMPLE.table
```


## Parameters for parallel execution

| Required                     | Note
| :----------------------------| :-
| `-tb [filename] `            | docking table (.table)


| Optional                  | default       | Note
| :------------------------ | :------------ | :-- 
| `-lg [filename]`          | master.log    | log filename
| `-rt [integer]`           | 0             | the number of retries


## Example of docking table (.table)

Parameters and docking target list should be written in a text file.
A table file should have `TITLE` and `PARAM` lines followed by parameters listed by the same order as in the `PARAM` line.
`SAMPLE.table` file in this package shows an example.

- [data/SAMPLE.table](data/SAMPLE.table)

```
TITLE=sample jobs
PARAM=-R $1 -L $2 -O
data/1gcq_r.pdb	data/1gcq_r.pdb
data/1gcq_r.pdb	data/1gcq_l.pdb
data/1gcq_l.pdb	data/1gcq_r.pdb
data/1gcq_l.pdb	data/1gcq_l.pdb
```

You can specify docking parameters loaded by MEGADOCK by setting `PARAM` in the table file.
Lines follows the `PARAM` lines specifies parameters for each docking job which will be distributed to available nodes by MPI.

### More details about parameters for each docking calculation

- [See above section](#Parametersfor-docking-calculation)

----

# Thread parallelization (OpenMP)

MEGADOCK parallelizes rotation calculations by using OpenMP.
You can specify the number of OpenMP threads for parallel calculations by environmental variable such as `$OMP_NUM_THREADS`.

```sh
# e.g.) megadock binary using 8 OpenMP threads
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=8
./megadock -R data/receptor.pdb -L data/ligand.pdb -o data/receptor_ligand.out

# e.g.) each MPI process uses 8 OpenMP threads
mpirun -n 4 -x OMP_NUM_THREADS=8  ./megadock-dp -tb data/SAMPLE.table
```

----


# Generate decoy from docking output

Each docking job generates docking output file in which rotation angles (x, y, z) of ligand from the initial structure, numbers of voxel translation (x, y, z) from receptor center coordinate and docking scores are listed.  

If you want to generate decoy pdbfiles, please use `decoygen` command. It is generated together with MEGADOCK binary.

## Command Usage

```sh
./decoygen [decoy_filename] [used_ligand.pdb] [.outfile] [decoy no.]
```


## Command Example

For example, the megadock output file was generated as `dock.out` using `rec.pdb` as receputer input and `lig.pdb` as ligand output, and you want to **generate 1st ranked decoy**.

```sh
# megadock docking calculation
megadock -R rec.pdb -L lig.pdb -o dock.out

# generate 1st ranked decoy
./decoygen lig.1.pdb lig.pdb dock.out 1
cat rec.pdb lig.1.pdb > decoy.1.pdb

# lig.1.pdb   : rotated and translated lig.pdb
# decoy.1.pdb : complex pdb file
```

If you want to generate all decoys;

```sh
# megadock docking calculation
megadock -R rec.pdb -L lig.pdb -o dock.out

# generate all decoys
for i in `seq 1 2000`; do ./decoygen lig.${i}.pdb lig.pdb dock.out $i; cat rec.pdb lig.${i}.pdb > decoy.${i}.pdb; done
```

----

# Blocking target residues

`block` tool (python script) is to block some residues of a receptor protein from docking.
If you know that some residues are not in the binding sides, please list their residue numbers and input `block` tool.
This program changes the name of residues to "BLK" and prints the new pdb on the screen.

```sh
./block [pdbfile] [chain] [target residue list]
# ex)
# ./block 1gcq_r.pdb B 182-186,189,195-198,204 > blocked.pdb
```

Target residues list is separated by commas and no spaces.
You can also use `-` (hyphen): "182-186" means blocking residues of 182, 183, ..., 186.
Blocked residues are substituted for 'BLK'.
Updated PDB coordinates are written to "standard output". MEGADOCK can only block receptor residues.

----

# Protein-Protein interaction prediction

You can calculates the evaluated value of Protein-Protein Interaction scores (PPI score) by using `ppiscore` command which is written in perl script.

## Command Example

```sh
# 1. Docking calculation using MEGADOCK with `-t=3` option
megadock -R rec.pdb -L lig.pdb -o dock.out -t 3 -N 10800

# -t: the number of predictions per each rotation
# -N: the number of output predictions


# 2. Output PPI score
./ppiscore dock.out 10800
```

### Note

`ppiscore` is compatible with re-ranking tools

to get better docking candidates (e.g. [ZRANK1](http://zdock.umassmed.edu/software/)) and those tools can be used for the output files of docking calculation using megadock.
If you want to use such reranking tools, please refer to [our website documentation](http://www.bi.cs.titech.ac.jp/megadock/ppi.html).

For more details about `ppiscore`, please check [our webpage documentation](http://www.bi.cs.titech.ac.jp/megadock/ppi.html) or following references.

----


## References

- Masahito Ohue, Takehiro Shimoda, Shuji Suzuki, Yuri Matsuzaki, Takashi Ishida, Yutaka Akiyama. MEGADOCK 4.0: an ultra-high-performance protein-protein docking software for heterogeneous supercomputers. Bioinformatics, 30(22), 3281-3283, 2014.

- Masahito Ohue, Yuri Matsuzaki, Nobuyuki Uchikoga, Takashi Ishida, Yutaka Akiyama. MEGADOCK: An all-to-all protein-protein interaction prediction system using tertiary structure data. Protein and Peptide Letters, 21(8), 766-778, 2014.

- Takehiro Shimoda, Takashi Ishida, Shuji Suzuki, Masahito Ohue, Yutaka Akiyama. MEGADOCK-GPU: An accelerated protein-protein docking calculation on GPUs. In Proc. ACM-BCB 2013 (ParBio Workshop 2013), 884-890, 2013.
 
- Yuri Matsuzaki, Nobuyuki Uchikoga, Masahito Ohue, Takehiro Shimoda, Toshiyuki Sato, Takashi Ishida, Yutaka Akiyama. MEGADOCK 3.0: A high-performance protein-protein interaction prediction software using hybrid parallel computing for petascale supercomputing environments. Source Code for Biology and Medicine, 8(1): 18, 2013.

- Masahito Ohue, Yuri Matsuzaki, Takashi Ishida, Yutaka Akiyama. Improvement of the Protein-Protein Docking Prediction by Introducing a Simple Hydrophobic Interaction Model: an Application to Interaction Pathway Analysis. Lecture Note in Bioinformatics 7632 (In Proc. of PRIB 2012), 178-187, Springer Heidelberg, 2012.

----

## Contact

- Email : megadock@bi.c.titech.ac.jp
- URL : http://www.bi.cs.titech.ac.jp/megadock

# Installation Guide


## Target Environments

| Type | Target Env.     | Approach           |
|:----:|-----------------|--------------------|
|  (a) | GPU cluster     | GPU + OpenMP + MPI |
|  (b) | CPU cluster     | OpenMP + MPI       |
|  (c) | GPU node        | GPU + OpenMP       |
|  (d) | CPU node        | OpenMP             |


## Requirement

| Library                                                         | GPU cluster | CPU cluster | GPU node | CPU node | Note |
|:----------------------------------------------------------------|:-----------:|:-----------:|:---:|:---:|:------|
| [FFTW3](http://www.fftw.org)                                    | yes           | yes           | yes   | yes   | `--enable-float` required ([FAQ](http://www.bi.cs.titech.ac.jp/megadock/faq.html))|
| MPI (e.g. [OpenMPI](http://www.open-mpi.org))                   | yes           | yes           |     |     |       |
| [CUDA Toolkit](https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-zone)          | yes           |             | yes   |     | `ver >= 5.0` required |
| [CUDA SDK code samples](https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-zone) | yes           |             | yes   |     | same version as toolkit |

For more detailed build information, please reffer to the [FAQ](http://www.bi.cs.titech.ac.jp/megadock/faq.html) page.


## Section Link

Please select appropriate section for your environment:

- [(a) Compile for GPU cluster (GPU & MPI)](#a-compile-for-gpu-cluster-gpu--mpi)
- [(b) Compile for MPI cluster (MPI)](#b-compile-for-mpi-cluster-mpi)
- [(c) Compile for GPU node (GPU)](#c-compile-for-gpu-node-gpu)
- [(d) Compile for CPU node (only thread parallelization)](#d-compile-for-cpu-node-only-thread-parallelization)

# Command Guide

This documentation show the command usage and examples for protein-protein docking calculation using MEGADOCK.
If you do not have any MEGADOCK binary, please read the build documentation ([doc/BUILD.md](./BUILD.md)).

> Note: The sample input files (`.pdb`, `.table`) are stored in `data` directory.


## Section Link

Please select your target environment and check the command example.

| Type | Target Env.     | Binary             | Note 
|:----:|-----------------|--------------------| :-
|  (a) | [GPU cluster](#command-for-multiple-nodes-environment) | `megadock-gpu-dp`  | multiple nodes
|  (b) | [CPU cluster](#command-for-multiple-nodes-environment) | `megadock-dp`      | multiple nodes
|  (c) | [GPU node](#command-for-single-node-environment)      | `megadock-gpu`     | single node
|  (d) | [CPU node](#command-for-single-node-environment)      | `megadock`         | single node

Other Commands:

| Command    | Note
| :-         | :-
| `decoygen` | [Generate decoy pdb files from docking output](#Generate-decoy-from-docking-output)
| `block`    | [Blocking target residues](#Blocking-target-residues)
| `ppiscore` | [Protein-Protein interaction prediction](#Protein-Protein-interaction-prediction)

# Command for Single Node Environment

Target Environments:
  - (c) Compile for GPU node (GPU)
  - (d) Compile for CPU node (only thread parallelization)

## Command example

```sh
# (c) GPU single node
./megadock-gpu -R receptor.pdb -L ligand.pdb -o receptor-ligand.out

# (d) CPU single node
./megadock -R receptor.pdb -L ligand.pdb -o receptor-ligand.out
```

### Run small sample

```sh
# (c) GPU single node
./megadock-gpu -R data/1gcq_r.pdb -L data/1gcq_l.pdb -o data/1gcq_r-1gcq_l.out

# (d) CPU single node
./megadock -R data/1gcq_r.pdb -L data/1gcq_l.pdb -o data/1gcq_r-1gcq_l.out
```

## Parameters for docking calculation

| Required            | Note
| :-------------------| :-
| `-R [filename]`     | receptor pdb file (input)
| `-L [filename]`     | ligand pdb file (input)


| Optional                  | default       | Note
| :------------------------ | :------------ | :-- 
| `-o [filename]`           | $R-$L.out     | output filename (output)
| `-O`                      |               | output docking detail files
| `-N [integer]`            | 2000          | set the number of output predictions
| `-t [integer]`            | 1             | set the number of predictions per each rotation
| `-F [integer]`            |               | set the number of FFT point (default: none)
| `-v [float]`              | 1.2 (angstrom)| set the voxel pitch size
| `-D`                      |               | set the 6 deg. (54000 angles) of rotational sampling (default to none, 15 deg. (3600 angles) of rotational sampling)
| `-r [integer]`            | 3600          | set the number of rotational sampling angles (54000: 54000 angles, 1: 1 angles, 24: 24 angles, default to 3600 angles)
| `-e [float]`              | 1.0           | set the electrostatics term ratio
| `-d [float]`              | 1.0           | set the hydrophobic term ratio
| `-a [float]`              | -45.0         | set the rPSC receptor core penalty
| `-b [float]`              | 1.0           | set the rPSC ligand core penalty
| `-f [1/2/3]`              | 3             | set function (1: rPSC only, 2: rPSC+Elec, 3: rPSC+Elec+RDE, default to 3)
| `-h`                      |               | show command help


----

# Command for Multiple Nodes Environment

Target Environments:
- (a) Compile for GPU cluster (GPU & MPI)
- (b) Compile for CPU cluster (MPI)

## Command example

```sh
# (a) GPU & MPI (e.g. 4 MPI processes)
mpirun -n 4 ./megadock-gpu-dp -tb data/SAMPLE.table

# (b) CPU & MPI (e.g. 4 MPI processes)
mpirun -n 4 ./megadock-dp -tb data/SAMPLE.table
```


## Parameters for parallel execution

| Required                     | Note
| :----------------------------| :-
| `-tb [filename] `            | docking table (.table)


| Optional                  | default       | Note
| :------------------------ | :------------ | :-- 
| `-lg [filename]`          | master.log    | log filename
| `-rt [integer]`           | 0             | the number of retries


## Example of docking table (.table)

Parameters and docking target list should be written in a text file.
A table file should have `TITLE` and `PARAM` lines followed by parameters listed by the same order as in the `PARAM` line.
`SAMPLE.table` file in this package shows an example.

- [data/SAMPLE.table](data/SAMPLE.table)

```
TITLE=sample jobs
PARAM=-R $1 -L $2 -O
data/1gcq_r.pdb	data/1gcq_r.pdb
data/1gcq_r.pdb	data/1gcq_l.pdb
data/1gcq_l.pdb	data/1gcq_r.pdb
data/1gcq_l.pdb	data/1gcq_l.pdb
```

You can specify docking parameters loaded by MEGADOCK by setting `PARAM` in the table file.
Lines follows the `PARAM` lines specifies parameters for each docking job which will be distributed to available nodes by MPI.

### More details about parameters for each docking calculation

- [See above section](#Parametersfor-docking-calculation)

----

# Thread parallelization (OpenMP)

MEGADOCK parallelizes rotation calculations by using OpenMP.
You can specify the number of OpenMP threads for parallel calculations by environmental variable such as `$OMP_NUM_THREADS`.

```sh
# e.g.) megadock binary using 8 OpenMP threads
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=8
./megadock -R data/receptor.pdb -L data/ligand.pdb -o data/receptor_ligand.out

# e.g.) each MPI process uses 8 OpenMP threads
mpirun -n 4 -x OMP_NUM_THREADS=8  ./megadock-dp -tb data/SAMPLE.table
```

----


# Generate decoy from docking output

Each docking job generates docking output file in which rotation angles (x, y, z) of ligand from the initial structure, numbers of voxel translation (x, y, z) from receptor center coordinate and docking scores are listed.  

If you want to generate decoy pdbfiles, please use `decoygen` command. It is generated together with MEGADOCK binary.

## Command Usage

```sh
./decoygen [decoy_filename] [used_ligand.pdb] [.outfile] [decoy no.]
```


## Command Example

For example, the megadock output file was generated as `dock.out` using `rec.pdb` as receputer input and `lig.pdb` as ligand output, and you want to **generate 1st ranked decoy**.

```sh
# megadock docking calculation
megadock -R rec.pdb -L lig.pdb -o dock.out

# generate 1st ranked decoy
./decoygen lig.1.pdb lig.pdb dock.out 1
cat rec.pdb lig.1.pdb > decoy.1.pdb

# lig.1.pdb   : rotated and translated lig.pdb
# decoy.1.pdb : complex pdb file
```

If you want to generate all decoys;

```sh
# megadock docking calculation
megadock -R rec.pdb -L lig.pdb -o dock.out

# generate all decoys
for i in `seq 1 2000`; do ./decoygen lig.${i}.pdb lig.pdb dock.out $i; cat rec.pdb lig.${i}.pdb > decoy.${i}.pdb; done
```

----

# Blocking target residues

`block` tool (python script) is to block some residues of a receptor protein from docking.
If you know that some residues are not in the binding sides, please list their residue numbers and input `block` tool.
This program changes the name of residues to "BLK" and prints the new pdb on the screen.

```sh
./block [pdbfile] [chain] [target residue list]
# ex)
# ./block 1gcq_r.pdb B 182-186,189,195-198,204 > blocked.pdb
```

Target residues list is separated by commas and no spaces.
You can also use `-` (hyphen): "182-186" means blocking residues of 182, 183, ..., 186.
Blocked residues are substituted for 'BLK'.
Updated PDB coordinates are written to "standard output". MEGADOCK can only block receptor residues.

----

# Protein-Protein interaction prediction

You can calculates the evaluated value of Protein-Protein Interaction scores (PPI score) by using `ppiscore` command which is written in perl script.

## Command Example

```sh
# 1. Docking calculation using MEGADOCK with `-t=3` option
megadock -R rec.pdb -L lig.pdb -o dock.out -t 3 -N 10800

# -t: the number of predictions per each rotation
# -N: the number of output predictions


# 2. Output PPI score
./ppiscore dock.out 10800
```

### Note

`ppiscore` is compatible with re-ranking tools to get better docking candidates (e.g. [ZRANK1](http://zdock.umassmed.edu/software/)) and those tools can be used for the output files of docking calculation using megadock.
If you want to use such reranking tools, please refer to [our website documentation](http://www.bi.cs.titech.ac.jp/megadock/ppi.html).

For more details about `ppiscore`, please check [our webpage documentation](http://www.bi.cs.titech.ac.jp/megadock/ppi.html) or following references.

{
  "option_title": "Agreement before interpreting acceleration or denser search",
  "question": "Do CPU and GPU standard docking agree across all 50 retained poses on four fixed cases after independent repeatability and error calibration?",
  "hypothesis": "Independent repeats and numerical error analysis can establish defensible CPU/GPU agreement before acceleration or denser search receives scientific interpretation.",
  "compute_axis": {
    "quantity": "Independent same-backend calibration executions per case and backend; cumulative levels, not search density",
    "unit": "repeats per case per backend",
    "levels": [2, 4]
  },
  "held_fixed": [
    "DESIGN, from requested protocol: exactly 1aua__A1_P24280--1aua__A2_P24280:apo; 1ax2__A1_P16404--1ax2__A2_P16404:apo; 1dv1__A1_P24182--1dv1__B1_P24182:apo; 1nr5__A1_P07547--1nr5__A2_P07547:apo. PINDER release 2024-02; no replacement cases.",
    "DESIGN source pins: MEGADOCK 9575280c875732553266e26adc607dd892b02616 and PINDER ebeb28a2f8411363cef722b7d293c978f7442672. Hash prepared inputs, native references, mappings, binaries, dependencies, build flags and image before execution. Public build routes: [build].",
    "DESIGN commands: OMP_NUM_THREADS=26 OMP_DYNAMIC=FALSE; megadock or megadock-gpu -R RECEPTOR -L LIGAND -o OUTPUT -N50 -t1 -v1.2 -e1 -d1 -a-45 -b1 -f3 -r3600. Explicit affinity and single allocated H100 PCIe; no concurrent docking jobs. Command interface and OpenMP documented in [commands].",
    "Calibration levels add independent process launches, retaining identical inputs/settings. No seeds varied without documented source support. Never change precision, scoring, ranking or retained count in scientific arms.",
    "Native references inaccessible to docking and calibration decisions. No -D, dense search, native scoring or quality selection in this card. Later rank1 and best50 DockQ remain separate."
  ],
  "predictions": {
    "if_lever": "Four repeats resolve agreement status for all four cases where two repeats leave numerical uncertainty.",
    "if_not": "Four repeats leave at least one case unresolved, or both repeat levels already give identical agreement status.",
    "decision_rule": "For each level seal casewise score/grid/coordinate tolerances from same-backend repeats plus independent numerical analysis before a fresh CPU/GPU pair. Pass requires 4/4 cases, 50/50 rows each, all structural checks and normalized errors <=1. Compute benefit only if level 2 is unresolved and level 4 resolves all cases without widening scientific requirements to fit cross-backend observations. Repeat-count result may be failure, not a compute lever.",
    "noise_rule": "Separate exact bytes from scientific equivalence. Compare repeat files bytewise after excluding volatile logs; never round away score differences. For science, derive per-component error bounds using traced operation precision, grid dimensions, FFT normalization, rounding/serialization and independent higher-precision checks on preselected synthetic inputs and sampled case grids. Add independently measured same-backend variability to that justified error budget. Audit top-50 boundary and adjacent score gaps; allow rank swaps only inside presealed overlapping score intervals with bijective transform/pose correspondence. Compare original rank rows and matched rows; require exact grid dimensions, atom identities and coordinate frames. Freeze numeric bounds and tie policy before fresh cross-backend output is opened. No justified bound means unresolved; no old maximum delta plus epsilon and no runtime ratio as tolerance.",
    "expected": "unsure",
    "expected_why": "Repeats can expose instability, but this plan has no independent error anchor yet and cannot predict whether additional repeats resolve it."
  },
  "compute_tested": "no",
  "compute_tested_why": "Necessary validation card. More executions buy evidence about agreement; this plan tests neither search-density gains nor parallel scheduling or throughput.",
  "scored_against": "CPU standard provides paired reference, not truth. Independent transform reconstruction, synthetic correlation checks and higher-precision error analysis validate mechanics; fresh CPU/GPU outputs face frozen casewise tolerances. Later native-reference DockQ is outside this card [pinder].",
  "arms": [
    {
      "id": "cpu_subset",
      "what": "First screen: four CPU-only unit commands, same historical settings, compared with supplied historical standard-CPU manifests; no GPU docking or native scoring."
    },
    {
      "id": "cpu_full_control",
      "what": "Conditional mismatch diagnosis: CPU-only full/control harness, same unit commands, no dense search or native scoring. Separate subset effects from baseline drift."
    },
    {
      "id": "repeat_calibration",
      "what": "Cumulative 2 then 4 independent standard runs per case per backend, isolated outputs and fixed settings; numerical analysis performed before any cross-backend verdict."
    },
    {
      "id": "fresh_pair",
      "what": "After calibration seal, one fresh CPU and GPU standard execution per case; compare every retained row, grid metadata and regenerated pose. No dense arm."
    }
  ],
  "baseline": {
    "what": "Pinned CPU standard: 3600 rotations, 50 retained predictions, 26 threads. Historical manifests are diagnostic references only; no historical score tolerance is accepted.",
    "value": "Fresh CPU output per case; historical material supplied later, unverified here."
  },
  "anchor": {
    "absent_reason": "No published numerical tolerance or independently reproduced code anchor exists in this plan. Build independent transform and synthetic-correlation checks plus precision/error analysis during calibration. Until these pass and numeric tolerances are sealed, scientific CPU/GPU agreement stays unavailable. Published scaling evidence [prior] is not an accuracy anchor."
  },
  "checks": [
    "Implement plan artifacts before any allocation: units.json, harness_from.json, commands.json, manifest.py, compare.py, calibration.json, controller.py and final report template. Preserve raw outputs and stable per-unit final PDB/docking-output hashes; put volatile logs in separate timing/activity records.",
    "CPU-only runner must allowlist four CPU-standard units and reject GPU, -D, native scoring and undocumented stages. Unit identity includes input hashes, command, backend, binary hash, environment and relative output names.",
    "Initial diagnostic acceptance: 0 stable-file byte mismatches. Equality supports repeat/subset assumption only. On mismatch compare subset with new full/control: their equality against a changed historical reference suggests baseline drift; their inequality suggests harness/subsetting differences. Report ambiguity and stop, never relax byte criterion.",
    "Scientific comparator: require finite scores, exactly 50 unique ranked rows, valid rotations/translations, correct voxel/grid metadata, complete atom correspondence and regenerated pose correspondence. Preserve original order, tie groups and all raw deltas.",
    "Reject malformed, duplicated, missing or reordered output in comparator fixtures. Independently reconstruct ligand rotation/translation, test identity and known synthetic transforms, and verify decoygen output [commands]. Generated test fixtures are design checks, not producer docking measurements.",
    "Build separate CPU/GPU binaries using documented routes; record FFTW float configuration, cuFFT/CUDA, compiler optimization and architecture choices [build]. Any portability patch changes binary identity and requires fresh calibration.",
    "Measure setup, retrieval, build, docking, pose generation, comparison, export and idle separately; sample GPU activity and record full allocation timestamps. Charge all elapsed instance time, including CPU-only work [billing].",
    "No new box workload while carding. No producer MEASURED pilot claimed. Private records remain user-supplied exploratory context; none was opened or publicly verified.",

No public URL validates these observations. Fresh work is prospective replication, never unseen holdout.",

{
  "option_title": "Agreement before interpreting acceleration or denser search",
  "question": "Do CPU and GPU standard docking agree across all 50 retained poses on four fixed cases after independent repeatability and error calibration?",

  "compute_axis": {

    "DESIGN, from requested protocol: exactly 1aua__A1_P24280--1aua__A2_P24280:apo; 1ax2__A1_P16404--1ax2__A2_P16404:apo; 1dv1__A1_P24182--1dv1__B1_P24182:apo; 1nr5__A1_P07547--1nr5__A2_P07547:apo. PINDER release 2024-02; no replacement cases.",
    "DESIGN source pins: MEGADOCK 9575280c875732553266e26adc607dd892b02616 and PINDER ebeb28a2f8411363cef722b7d293c978f7442672. Hash prepared inputs, native references, mappings, binaries, dependencies, build flags and image before execution. Public build routes: [build].",
    "DESIGN commands: OMP_NUM_THREADS=26 OMP_DYNAMIC=FALSE; megadock or megadock-gpu -R RECEPTOR -L LIGAND -o OUTPUT -N50 -t1 -v1.2 -e1 -d1 -a-45 -b1 -f3 -r3600. Explicit affinity and single allocated H100 PCIe; no concurrent docking jobs. Command interface and OpenMP documented in [commands].",
    "Calibration levels add independent process launches, retaining identical inputs/settings. No seeds varied without documented source support. Never change precision, scoring, ranking or retained count in scientific arms.",
    "Native references inaccessible to docking and calibration decisions. No -D, dense search, native scoring or quality selection in this card. Later rank1 and best50 DockQ remain separate."
  ],
  "predictions": {
    "if_lever": "Four repeats resolve agreement status for all four cases where two repeats leave numerical uncertainty.",
    "if_not": "Four repeats leave at least one case unresolved, or both repeat levels already give identical agreement status.",
    "decision_rule": "For each level seal casewise score/grid/coordinate tolerances from same-backend repeats plus independent numerical analysis before a fresh CPU/GPU pair. Pass requires 4/4 cases, 50/50 rows each, all structural checks and normalized errors <=1. Compute benefit only if level 2 is unresolved and level 4 resolves all cases without widening scientific requirements to fit cross-backend observations. Repeat-count result may be failure, not a compute lever.",

For science, derive per-component error bounds using traced operation precision, grid dimensions, FFT normalization, rounding/serialization and independent higher-precision checks on preselected synthetic inputs and sampled case grids. Add independently measured same-backend variability to that justified error budget. Audit top-50 boundary and adjacent score gaps; allow rank swaps only inside presealed overlapping score intervals with bijective transform/pose correspondence. Compare original rank rows and matched rows; require exact grid dimensions, atom identities and coordinate frames. Freeze numeric bounds and tie policy before fresh cross-backend output is opened. No justified bound means unresolved; no old maximum delta plus epsilon and no runtime ratio as tolerance.",
